name: Relationships
blurb: Who built what, what trained on what, what cites what, and what regulates what.

edges.method: arXiv ids the model authors put in their own Hub tags
defendant matching against the CourtListener docket tracker
publisher matching against the official MCP registry

reading.body:
The site's knowledge graph contains 25,891 recorded edges across eleven distinct relationship types, connecting models, papers, companies, people, and regulatory filings into a single queryable structure as of September 2026.

The largest edges by count are also the most technically grounded. Models citing papers accounts for 8,602 edges, sourced from arXiv identifiers that model authors placed in their own Hub tags, meaning the provenance comes from the authors themselves rather than from external inference. Model-to-modality assignments account for another 16,369 edges, derived from the Hub's own pipeline and tag filters. Together these two types represent roughly 96 percent of all edges, which means the graph's mass is concentrated in the technology layer, not the legal or commercial one.

The remaining nine edge types cover legal exposure, capital formation, intellectual property, and market presence. Seventy-two companies appear as defendants in tracked lawsuits, 122 have filed Form D disclosures matched against SEC EDGAR, 108 hold granted patents matched against USPTO records, and 37 are verified SEC registrants. These counts describe floors, not ceilings, because each method notes only what could be matched with confidence. The 12 APIs tracked by live status polling and the 28 vendor feeds mapped to companies are small in count but structurally different from the rest: they update continuously rather than being fixed at a point in time.

What this data does not cover is causation or weight. An edge records that a relationship exists, not how significant it is. A model citing a paper eight times and a model citing it once are both single edges. The graph is a map of connections, and interpreting which connections matter requires the pages those edges point to.
